generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

For the data with the following summaries:

  • \(n = {@n@}\)
  • \( \sum{x}= {@sum_x@}\)
  • \( \sum{y} = {@sum_y@}\)
  • \( \sum{xy} = {@sum_xy@}\)
  • \( \sum{x^2} = {@sum_x2@}\)
  • \(\sum{y^2} = {@sum_y2@}\)

To find the equation of the regression line for \(Y\) on \(X\) and \(X\) on \(Y\), we can use the formulas for the slope \((b\) or \(\beta)\) and the intercept \((a\) or \(\alpha)\) of the regression lines. The formulas for simple linear regression are as follows:


a) For \(\textbf{Y}\) on \(\textbf{X}\), given by \(\textbf{Y}=a+b\textbf{X}\)

\( \displaystyle b = \frac{n\sum{xy} - (\sum{x})(\sum{y})}{n\sum{x^2} - (\sum{x})^2}\)

\( \displaystyle b ={@b@} \)

\(b \approx {@decimalplaces(b,2)@} \)

Now, calculate \(a\):

\( \displaystyle a = \frac{\sum{y} - b\sum{x}}{n}\)

\( \displaystyle a ={@a@} \)

\(a \approx {@decimalplaces(a,2)@} \)

So, the equation for \(\textbf{Y}\) on \(\textbf{X}\) is approximately:

\( \displaystyle \textbf{Y} ={@ta1@} \)

\(\textbf{Y} \approx {@alt_ta1@}\)


b) For \(\textbf{X}\) on \(\textbf{Y}\), given by \(\textbf{X}=\alpha + \beta \textbf{Y}\)

\( \displaystyle \beta = \frac{n\sum{xy} -( \sum{x})(\sum{y})}{n\sum{y^2} - (\sum{y})^2}\)

\( \displaystyle \beta ={@beta@} \)

\( \beta \approx {@decimalplaces(beta,2)@} \)

Now, calculate α:

\( \displaystyle \alpha = \frac{\sum{x} - \beta\sum{y}}{n}\)

\(\displaystyle \alpha ={@alpha@} \)

\( \alpha \approx {@decimalplaces(alpha,2)@} \)

So, the equation for \(\textbf{X}\) on \(\textbf{Y}\) is approximately:

\( \displaystyle \textbf{X} ={@ta2@} \)

\(\textbf{X} \approx {@alt_ta2@} \)
